blocks.p: You run a wholesale bakery. Hotels and cafes order every week, and every invoice goes out with a due date.
Your cash forecast is a spreadsheet, and it assumes every client pays on that date. But one of your biggest clients pays about six weeks late.

blocks.b: The spreadsheet says you're fine. You're not.

blocks.p: In week six, the staff bonus, payroll and insurance all come due: $188,900 in a single week.
The late client's payment hasn't arrived, but the spreadsheet counts it as already paid, so nothing warns you.

blocks.b: One late payment becomes a cash gap, and nobody sees it coming.

blocks.p: What if the forecast learned how each client really pays?
That's what EXERGY built as a proof of concept: Cash Gap Forecaster. It reads three years of invoices and payments, then draws the next 13 weeks.
Week six closes at $19,934, $10,066 under the minimum. Move the staff bonus back two weeks and it becomes $102,934.

blocks.b: You test the fix before you commit.

blocks.text: Uses three years of invoices and payments to learn how each client really pays.
Flags the week cash drops below your minimum, over a month ahead.
Move a bill and see the new forecast before you commit.
Shows ranges and marks what is an estimate.

blocks.b: A forecast you can check, question, and test.
